subsystem: Channels and remote access (Telegram, Discord, Slack, Signal, WhatsApp, SMS/phone, email, calendar, relay, car, devices, IoT, browser extension)
summary: Apex can be reached through many channels: Telegram, Discord, Slack, WhatsApp, Signal, SMS and phone calls through Twilio, a cloud relay with a phone page, the car page over Tailscale, Web Push, Home Assistant and a browser extension. The code is careful about security (signed webhooks, allowlists that refuse everyone by default) and is wired the same way in main.py and in your resident launcher. But every channel is off until you add accounts and keys, none of them has run on your laptop, and most need a public HTTPS address you don't have. For you in Lebanon the realistic paths are Telegram in polling mode, Pairing over Tailscale, and later the relay. There are real bugs: SMS/WhatsApp freeze the dashboard while Apex thinks, Telegram replies can vanish on bad Markdown, the browser extension needs a dashboard token, Apex can't switch Home Assistant devices by itself, and the email, calendar and phone panels in the dashboard are dead code.

gaps.issue: SMS and WhatsApp webhooks run the whole Apex turn synchronously inside an async handler. While Apex thinks, the dashboard's event loop is frozen (companion, WebSockets, other requests stall), and any turn longer than Twilio's ~15 s webhook timeout loses the reply. Telegram, Slack and Signal correctly use run_in_executor; Call Apex correctly uses a background thread.
gaps.evidence: dashboard/server.py:781-791 (twilio_inbound_sms calls phone_mod.dispatch_inbound_sms directly), dashboard/server.py:912-920 (whatsapp), tools/phone.py:94-98, tools/whatsapp.py:104-110; contrast dashboard/server.py:835 and 899
gaps.fix_hint: Ack immediately with empty TwiML and send the reply with sms_send/whatsapp send_message from a worker thread (same pattern as Call Apex's text_later).
gaps.how_confirmed: Re-read both async handlers: no await/run_in_executor around the dispatch call, and dispatch calls _agent_run_fn inline; compared with the Telegram/Slack/Signal handlers which hand off to an executor.

gaps.issue: Browser extension cannot send anything unless DASHBOARD_TOKEN is set: the middleware rejects every POST from a chrome-extension:// origin that is not bearer-authenticated, and with no token configured nothing is ever bearer-authenticated. The README implies a local http://localhost:7860 setup works.
gaps.fix_hint: Document that a device token is required (and pre-fill one via the pairing link), or allow extension origins on loopback when no token is configured.
gaps.how_confirmed: Ran a TestClient snippet: POST with Origin chrome-extension://abcdef and DASHBOARD_TOKEN='' returned 403 'Use the same origin as your Apex dashboard.'; with a token and matching Bearer it passed the middleware (404 for the dummy path).

gaps.issue: Telegram replies are sent with parse_mode=Markdown and no plain-text retry. Model replies often contain unbalanced _ or * (file names, snake_case, bullet stars); Telegram then refuses the message with 'can't parse entities' and you simply get no answer, only a line in the log.
gaps.evidence: tools/telegram.py:59-80 (parse_mode Markdown, error returned as string), tools/telegram.py:214 (result ignored)
gaps.fix_hint: On an API error mentioning entities, resend without parse_mode (or escape/use MarkdownV2 properly).
gaps.how_confirmed: Read send_message and dispatch_inbound: single request with parse_mode='Markdown', failure only returns '[Telegram] API error' which dispatch_inbound discards. The Telegram API's rejection of malformed Markdown is documented behaviour, not run here.

gaps.issue: Webhooks without a secret trust any loopback/private peer. Behind a tunnel running on the laptop (cloudflared, as docs/OMNIPRESENCE.md recommends, or tailscale serve/funnel) all internet traffic arrives from 127.0.0.1, so Telegram/Signal/IoT webhooks with no secret accept forged posts from anyone. The body's chat ID / number is the attacker's to choose, so knowing your Telegram chat ID would let a stranger run Apex as you; IoT with an empty allowlist accepts any entity.
gaps.evidence: dashboard/webhook_auth.py:43-71 (peer_is_local used as the escape hatch), 129-141 (telegram), 144-160 (signal), 163-178 (iot); docs/OMNIPRESENCE.md:26, 63-84
gaps.fix_hint: When PUBLIC_BASE_URL/TWILIO_PUBLIC_BASE_URL is set or a forwarded header is present, stop treating loopback as trusted; or require the secret whenever the channel is configured. Print a loud warning in the startup audit for local-only channels when a tunnel URL is configured.
gaps.how_confirmed: Read peer_is_local/_require and each verify_* function: with no secret they return early for loopback peers; read OMNIPRESENCE which tells you to keep Apex on 127.0.0.1 behind a local tunnel. Not exploitable on the laptop today because no tunnel or channel is configured.

gaps.issue: Apex cannot control Home Assistant by itself: iot_call_service, iot_get_state and iot_notify exist in tools/iot.py but are not declared as agent tools or dispatched in agent/core.py, so the safety rules written for iot_call_service never fire. Control only works through a separately configured Home Assistant MCP server (mcp__hass*).
gaps.fix_hint: Register the three functions as agent tools (with the safety rules) or delete them and point the docs at the HA MCP server.
gaps.how_confirmed: grep for iot_call_service/iot_get_state/iot_notify across agent/, tools/, dashboard/, app/ and main.py found only their definitions and the safety.py rules.

gaps.issue: Email inbox, calendar and phone/SMS panels in the dashboard are dead code: loadInbox, loadCalendar and loadPhone are never called and the elements they draw into (inbox-list, cal-range, phone-state, sms-form) exist in no HTML page. The /api/email/*, /api/calendar/events and /api/phone/* routes have no page.
gaps.fix_hint: Either add Inbox/Calendar/Phone sections to a page or delete the dead functions so nobody thinks they exist.
gaps.how_confirmed: grep -rlE 'inbox-list|cal-range|phone-state|sms-form' dashboard/ matched only app.js; grep for callers of loadPhone/loadInbox/loadCalendar found none.

gaps.issue: IoT inbound allowlist is allow-all when empty, unlike every other channel (deny-by-default).
gaps.fix_hint: Make an empty IOT_TRIGGER_ALLOWED_ENTITIES deny everything.
gaps.how_confirmed: Ran: tools.iot._is_allowed('lock.front_door') with an empty list returned True; telegram._is_allowed(123) with an empty list returned False.

gaps.issue: Email and calendar have no tests at all; Slack, WhatsApp and Signal message handling (dispatch) is untested beyond allowlist and signature checks.
gaps.evidence: tests/ (no file references email_box, calendar_box, slack.dispatch_event, whatsapp/signal dispatch_inbound)
gaps.fix_hint: Add fake-IMAP/CalDAV tests and dispatch tests with a stub agent.

gaps.issue: IoT on/off can only be toggled by typing /iot in main.py's text mode or by a raw POST to /api/iot/toggle; resident mode (the owner's launcher) has no command, tray item or page button for it.

gaps.how_confirmed: grep for '/iot' in app/resident.py and 'api/iot' in dashboard/static returned nothing.

gaps.issue: Telegram webhook registration helper set_webhook() is never called by any command or page, so webhook mode must be registered by hand (polling mode is the practical choice on the laptop anyway).
gaps.fix_hint: Expose it as a CLI (python -m tools.telegram --set-webhook) or remove it.

gaps.issue: Stale docstring: tools/signal.py says a blank SIGNAL_ALLOWED_NUMBERS allows anyone; the code denies everyone.
Tunnel scripts are bash (.sh) only; the owner's Windows laptop has no one-click way to get a public HTTPS address, which Discord, Slack, WhatsApp, SMS and Telegram-webhook all need.
gaps.fix_hint: Prefer Telegram polling and the cloud relay for Lebanon; add a .cmd for cloudflared only if a public URL is really wanted.
gaps.how_confirmed: ls scripts | grep tunnel showed only .sh files.

gaps.issue: Outlook/Hotmail addresses default to password IMAP/SMTP, which Microsoft has largely switched off for personal accounts in favour of OAuth; email may fail to log in for those addresses.
gaps.fix_hint: Document Gmail app passwords as the supported path, or add OAuth.
gaps.how_confirmed: Not tested; based on Microsoft's published basic-auth retirement, not on this code failing.

needs_from_owner: Decide which channel you actually want first. Recommended: Telegram in polling mode (no public address, works on slow internet). Create a bot with @BotFather, put TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN, TELEGRAM_ALLOWED_CHAT_IDS and TELEGRAM_POLLING=true in .env, restart with Start-Apex-Platform.cmd, then message the bot and confirm a reply arrives.
Set DASHBOARD_TOKEN in .env (Setup-Apex-Car.cmd offers to) before using the phone, the car page or the browser extension; the extension cannot work without it.
Install Tailscale on the laptop and phone, run Setup-Apex-Car.cmd, and check that the printed https://...ts.net/drive address opens on the phone and Celine answers.
Check the Apex startup log for the webhook audit lines (one per channel) and paste them back, so we know what is exposed.

If you want 'Call Apex' or the relay: it needs a paid Twilio number and a cloud server (VPS or Railway) with Tailscale; tell me whether that is worth paying for given power cuts and internet in Lebanon.
For email: tell me which provider; Gmail with an app password is the tested-in-principle path.
If you have Home Assistant at home, say so; otherwise IoT can stay off.

rating.why: Well-secured and wired identically in both launch modes with ~340 tests, but everything is off by default, nothing has run on the laptop, most channels need a public address and paid accounts, and there are real bugs (blocking SMS/WhatsApp, lost Telegram replies, extension 403, no HA control, dead dashboard panels).
